Science was once alive, that is to say, it was organized in the least of its sections in body, soul and spirit, and that alongside the physical part, the corpse, there was always a metaphysical part. The study of science was therefore as much a religious question as an intellectual one, and the works of the oratory supported and illuminated the work of the laboratory. This is the reason for the sanctuaries of Egypt and the title of priest which the learned men honored themselves with. Each science, constituted in Thesis, Antithesis and Synthesis, really lived in a complete Mathesis. All these words will seem incomprehensible to many contemporaries; so we will explain them as best we can. Let us take as an example V Alchemy, to say that TAlchemy is the first beginning of healthy chemistry is to listen to the reveries of encyclopedists and their successors and replace Tserious investigation with sound sentences.
In ancient sanctuariesnature was studied in its body, in its life, and in its
Spirit, and the whole was one and the same science. The study of the body taught the laws of

Universal organization, both social and natural; Study of Life enabled us to grasp the laws of transformation and gave the adept the power to transmute base metals into perfect metals and wild animals and plants plant animals usable for man; finally the study of the Spirit enabled us to grasp the laws of creation and gave the adept the power, not only to transform, but to create certain living beings.
XVP In the 14th, 15th and especially centuries of our era, a reaction, long threatening, occurred gradually. The whole part
Physics of science, everything that related to the corpse became the exclusive object of Vetude. of the official schools of science and the whole metaphysical part
(Life and Spirit) was rejected far from the official centers of teaching under the name of Occult Sciences.
(i) Voy. the Homuncules of O Kueffestein in the Revue L'Initiation of March 8, 1897.

Thus the whole physical part of Chemistry, that which led to the anatomy of the body of Nature and the classification of its constituent elements, that which was reserved for laboratory boys and beginners, remained the only one studied in the schools, and the whole metaphysical and living part was relegated to oblivion under the name of Alchemy, the name which the Arabs gave to the whole of Chemical Science. But we must not believe that living science ceased to be studied for this purpose. JoUivet Castelot shows us the opposite very well in his beautiful work. The secret societies of initiates preserved intact and alive the Kabbalistic traditions constituted in bodies (or Massora), in doubly polarized life (Mishna-Ghemarah) and in Spirit (High Kabbalah: Bereschit-Mercavah-Tarot). In the same way Nature was studied in these secret centers by the Chemist (i degree), by the Alchemist (2 degree) and by the Hermetic Philosopher (3 degree). The Tarot (Thôra-Rota), as very well understood and shown by M. Jollivet Castelot, served as the key to universal transposition for the three orders of study. As long as the chemists, these rebellious laboratory boys, were content to make

XIV classifications, they were able to despise their masters; but, from the day when they wished to make the philosophy of their science, they were obliged to return to the fold and recognize that those whom they called “those dreamers, these children, these fools of alchemists” possessed alone and from all antiquity this key of the unity of matter and of the plan of organization of Nature, after which the modern scientists always run. Initiated as a martinist in 1882, I had the great pleasure of being called to alchemical initiation in July 1883. My friend, Mr. JoUivet Castelot, will forgive me for asking him for a few pages to reproduce this document which I received on July 2, 1883 and which I publish for the first time; he had very much interested my dear Poisson, so cruelly removed from our affection. Man. You wanted to know our faith; you wanted to be one of us. Our door is not closed; it is open to all who know how to enter the temple. We have no priests, and you may as well come to the faith alone as by the help of an adept. Our duty is to show you the way. You have to follow her alone afterwards.

Listen. You don’t know anything and you want to learn. Why not? You are unhappy and you want to be happy. You believe that science will give you the happiness you desire; you believe, through work, to overcome the boredom that oppresses you.
Listen.
All this is true.
We can be happy, but we must not believe that science, the true
Science will make you happy by money; you must not come to us if you want a science that will lead you to honors.

If you are counting on Science to “come”, go to the Faculties. There you will be taught all that it takes to be many things if you want to work; by this you will reach dignities, but never happiness. Jealousy and ambition will overtake you; you will spend your life in continual anger, not knowing against whom or against what to rebel against. You will suffer as much as you can in your mind, for you will profess. If you are independent, you will be unhappy, because you will feel that what you are being told is false. If you are submissive, you will be unhappy, for you will see that when you reach the highest honors you are as unhappy as before.

"The happiness you were looking for when you were young, you will still be looking for it when you are old, and, lost in the mazes of present-day science, you will always feel when you see the Natute that you are missing something. Listen. The true adept must be independent. Alchemy will not give you bodily wealth; it will give you a more lasting fortune, a fortune that misfortunes cannot shake, spiritual wealth. As long as you suffer you will always be happy only the learned man eaten up by jealousy or pride and the rich man eaten up by boredom. Boredom, ambition, and pride will flee from you, and thereby you will be superior to all men. If you are not wealthy, you will live by working, but you will not reveal the secrets you have grasped. Each day will bring you a new batch of intellectual wealth, and your work will seem easier every day. Soon you will be able to work less for men and more for the Faith, and your tastes will be modest enough in happiness to satisfy you with little. Do not think that my words are baseless. If you ask me, I will quote you.

the example of more than two thousand of ours who lived calm and modest in the midst of the cruelest wars, in the midst of the most distressed centuries, and always happiness smiled at their wishes. Then, when you come to this height of intellectual happiness, when you see God manifesting Himself to you, when you are just and wise, for whatever modest employment you hold among men, you will always be superior to the official scholar. Both roads are open to you: you can choose. I repeat to you that we can give you no material well-being; we can only grant you spiritual happiness. Listen. Before you enter the book of God, you have to look at men. Look at this friend who sells his friend for gold; look at these men who destroy themselves for gold; look at the priests who are consumed by the ambition of honors; look at this doctor who kills men to earn more and not to confess powerless; look around you: you will see everywhere only the hunt for Tor. You came to us, believing that you were richer. Do you think then, madman, that we too have thrown ourselves into the current that leads to despair?

Do you think that alchemists are as unhappy as other men? I say to you that we are happy in the midst of all the miserable feverish people of today; do not therefore believe that we are thinking of gold.

And the true adepts who have found this secret in lafoLile, as evidenced by the gold coins still exhibited today in foreign museums, these adepts, I say, died without bequeathing their secret, for they knew too much about men. If transmutation exists, the adept does not dream it for the wealth it will provide. He dreams it because it is another opportunity for him to be close to God and to pray to Him.

p: We have no need here to examine the various theories which have been put forth on Matter,

Strength and molecules, then atoms; we do not make the history of the question; we will be content to consider the broad lines of the problem, the solution that is imposed on the science of today; addressing already educated readers, aware of these doctrines, we do nothing but recall them, referring to our previous works those who would like to deepen the chapter.
We must suppose admitted for the most part, in theory, the Unity of Matter, of Substance, the dynamical system known to the Egyptians and the Greeks.
Hindus initiated from antiquity, called Idealistne: but we prefer the term Dynamism much more scientific.
So this is only a sketch presented here, for the general clarity of the hermetic system.
The true atomic system is based on the Aether (Akasa-astral light, that is to say universal fluid of the Kabbalists, which our readers know) and the principle of Evolution.

It is the only rational system in accord with the idea of the Infinite, with the obvious presence of ethereal ripple. Matter, or what we call it, which seems to us to be an entity resistant and independent of the Force, although it is not so.

in reality, as we shall establish it is composed of molecules; these molecules are formed of almost infinitesimal particles: the chemical or material atotnes; but this atom already represents a degree of evolution of the Ether; it is not the germ, the material seed, the atom is constituted by the particles of Ether.
(See Lothar-Meyer: The Modern Theories of
Chemistry, edition; Lodge: Théories Modernes l'Electricité; Gaudin: Le Monde des Atomes.)

Ilyac therefore other atoms in reality than the chemical or agglomerated atom; these other atoms are the ethereal particles, of different uses, divisible to infinity, they, germs of the Evolutionary Matter containing in them the first evolutionary principle.
From their meeting is born Vaiome chemical basis of the others and complex combinations, stable point and probably (but not surely) unalterable under the pressures of the medium.

Therefore, we see that nothing prevents Matter from being infinitely divisible, admitting a kind of fixed point which is chemical Vatom, since Ether is Matter in an almost Jluidic state, matter formed of ever more infinitesimal particles. Formed by the Ether, the Atom is oriented, caused by the Ether.
Therefore a negative period succeeding a positive period (ether containing electricity in its two vibratory forms).
And we see that the Ether (the astral light of the Kabbalists, let us not forget it) is of the
Matter the almost fluidic state; that is to say, in the end, of compacted Venergy: the Aether is reduced to energy, as proved by the scientists who came to the Unity of forces.

One Energy manifests itself in various ways, according to its degree of compaction or its number of etheric particles. It is always the same Energy, but in the form of heat light, electricity, magnetism, sound, etc. , etc., or if one prefers, it is always the Force under the appearance of various energies resulting from the compaction of this Force.
So we arrive, solving everything, everything.

We have studied in the first part of this treatise the immutable as well as indispensable relations that exist between Kabbalistic Tradition and Alchemy. This has shown us the greatness of Hermetic Philosophy, which, rooted in the Alchemical specialty, rises, through Analogy as well as through Experience, to the most complex universal or Metaphysical problems. It would therefore be quite wrong to consider Hermeticism as the Art only of transmuting metals, the alchemist as a mere experimenter of the physical order. In reality, the mutation of bodies into each other is only the material consequence of the Principles and Laws revealed by the
The doctrine of Hermes, a true alchemist, a priest of Nature, obtains the Science of Transmutation only after he has proved himself worthy to possess it, by his moral or magical efforts.

The Blower of Antiquity and the Middle Ages, the chemist of our days, have no right whatsoever to the title of alchemist, of hermetic philosopher, for they ignore the teachings of Sacred Science, cannot boast of any slow and regular Initiation, for they consequently succeed in producing any complete transmutatory phenomenon, unless by intuition, very rarely and partially, their own High-mindedness, when they have made their own Truth.

The first condition that the aspirant to alchemical science must fulfill, if he wants to attempt to rise to VAdeptat, if he wants to be worthy to bear the name of Alchemist or Hermetic Philosopher, is to call himself Initiate, to prove himself: Mage.

The Alchemist must first be a mage, a necessity indispensable for attaining the perfect Ascesis, the Adeptate in its integrity, enabling him to obtain the facts pertaining to the strictly alchemical order.
"Bill is evident that this is a heavy task to be undertaken; it requires persevering and arduous efforts. Because one does not become a Mage-Alchemist in a few months, much less Adept.
The Adept representing the Magus reached the ultimate level of Knowledge, one conceives of the sum of works, of struggles, of success that it will have had to undergo and to win.
We can affirm that few adepts meet in the history of humanity, and that, for many called, there are very few elected.
All of us can, we must.
sooner or later achieve this grandiose goal of Adept or Messiah, according to the laws of our destiny and our abilities.
All of us carry within our souls the germ that will have to develop and give us back a Krishna, a Moses, a Hermes or a Pythagoras.
Our soul is like a diamond enclosed in its thick gangue, from which it must be extracted by incessant efforts; then it must be cut, polished, so that it projects all its fires.
But to realize this Work, the true Great Perfect Work, a very long time seems necessary, which will require many of our planetary existences.

Our readers know the Dogma of Reincarnation; we will not stop; these preliminaries were for the sole reason of indicating the necessity of Initiation, and now we will continue the exposition of the Magical Ascesis towards Adeptate.

Let us first support our assertions on the ancient texts, in order to prove well the reality of what we are advancing: that is to say, that the alchemist is only a specialist in Occult Science, and that he is not worthy to produce perfectly the phenomena of material transmutation unless he has reached Adeptate or the general Knowledge of the Magical Synthesis. The knowledge of Sacred Art, that is to say, of Alchemy, could only be communicated to the sons of kings, like Magic, for it was indeed there.
Priestly and Royal Art, of which the Adepts really became the Masters of the World.

Clement of Alexandria also says: Priests do not communicate their mysteries to anyone, reserving them for the heir to the throne or for those of them who excel in virtue and wisdom. The use of initiations was universal in antiquity. The Alchemists swore not to divulge the science revealed to them. Let us confine ourselves to indicating the principal seats of the great hermetic sanctuaries of Ancient Egypt, the alchemical laboratories from which the knowledge of the Magi, the experimental science of Transmutation, was drawn. They were: the land of Thebaid, Heracleopolis, Lycopolis, Aphrodite, Apollinopolis, Elephantine, Pthah and Serapis afterwards. In those mysterious colleges whose entrance was absolutely forbidden to the profane, where one penetrated only after rigorous and terrible trials, one formed, with a care that one no longer imagines in our century of egoism, enjoyment and lucre, Alchemists, future Adepts, disinterested, laborious, silent; the old Magi communicated to them some principles of self-interest.
Sacred Science, but above all, let their initiative develop their Soul, their
Intelligence.
For, as we know, the Initiation does not give itself: the neophyte must initiate himself, rise to the Truth by his own efforts, find in himself alone the Light.
Individual development: this is the law of Initiation.

And for very long years, the Alchemists lived cloistered in the sanctuaries that we have just mentioned: sometimes they tried the works of Transmutation and Chemistry, in the dark laboratories of the Temple; sometimes they studied the venerable and hieroglyphic texts and then parcou; in the beautiful gardens of the sanctuaries where Nature spread her magnificence, they meditated, dreamed also of the sun.
Poets who shuddered intellectually at the slightest initiatic breaths of the splendid Isis.

Silence; and it was only after having gone through all the stages of their speciality, that they abandoned the College, spread throughout the World in order to fashion in their turn, some work of science and art, or some novice soul. It was the theurge; the other went into the midst of the sick and wounded, and drove out suffering; it was the therapist, who was often doubled with the thaumaturge. Was it only a question of acting directly on Nature and no longer on Humanity, the Magus commanded the intellectual forces of the physical plane, and made springs spring into barren land or dematerialized the blocks of granite; the hennetist, therapist of Nature, created by his science the precious metals which enriched the College of the Wise and gave him the necessary means of action.

The list of these adaptations would be too long, if they had to be reviewed all over again; what we want to make clear is that all the specialists translated to the Crowd, in different forms, one and the same Great Principle that they had at first penetrated well. What was the result of this method?

It is that the characters used by the different adaptations all deriving from the same center and as a result of the same General Law, could be used by all the adapters in simply changing 1& meaning of the sign following each speculization, but without changing this sign itself. Thus a point in a circle was a sign common to all Initiates in their different adaptations.

For the theurgist, he meant the concentration of the divine force (the point) out of his multiple realizations (the circle). For the therapist, it indicated the healing soul (the point) within the Plant and the Matter that encloses it (the circle). The Mage saw his situation (the point) in the center of the insulator circle, while the Hermetist saw the perfect gold and the Astrologer recognized in him the Sun in all his analogies. Conversely, it was enough for an Initiate, whatever his speculation, to write a sign, for all the other initiates to understand this sign and immediately see its application to their own speciality. Hermetic science had as its special object the explanation of these signs in their most usual adaptations. After the destruction by Rome of the great universities of Egypt, the initiatory centers were postponed far to the East, and it is only long after, towards the Middle Ages, from the twelfth to the sixteenth century, that we will find in the West rare initiates engaged in the study of Hermeticism and generally known to the lay public under the name of Alchemists, name coming from the Arabic language. It is not to be confused with the Alchemists – true initiates knowing V Unity, who are pro-89premently speaking of the philosophers doing Chemistry, with the blowers, ignorant and rude people who are simply chemists of the time trying to do Philosophy. The naïve who have the faith of the Encyclopaedias, say that Alchemy gave birth to present-day Chemistry, committing a gross error. Some experiments of the laboratory of the Alchemists, redone without understanding the philosophical raison d'être, by the blowers and taken up later, during the renaissance, by the pharmacists of the time, have constituted a collection of formulas whose laws have been sought to classify under the name of Chemistry. Chemistry is a laboratory boy science for the Hermetic Philosopher, and opinion on this subject has not changed for the initiates from the 13th century to the present day. It does not matter that these laboratory boys invaded the salons and formed themselves into an Academy. Whenever they wanted to do the Philosophy of Chemistry, they were obliged to recognize that they could only take up the immutable teachings of their masters, the alchemists, because these masters alone possess the eternal principles that allow them on occasion to transform Matter by the processes of the laboratory but; this was an application for the future.

Hermetic philosophy, which would never have thought of going back from the facts of the laboratory to the world of the first laws; for its course was quite opposite: the laboratory, for the alchemist, was never but the consequence of the oratory.

It will no longer be surprising, after reading these pages, to see the great role that the alchemist must play, worthy of the name, and the rigorous conditions that such a goal requires. It will then be understood that the desired Asceticism is not a game, an easy trial of some time, but a slow priestly initiation; this priesthood has not ceased since the antiquity of the sanctuaries, and every man who aspires to become an Adept must receive the sacred characters; we will therefore continue these practical notes of magical training, defining the general principles that will allow to direct the Spirit towards the dazzling sources of Truth. Those of the confreres who know each other in any manner whatsoever, and of whatever colony or assembly they may be, may join and assemble together, to confer, when and as often as they may find fit, in certain assigned days and places. Catechism or instruction for the rank of Adept or Apprentice Sublime and Unknown Philosopher. What is the first study of a philosopher? It is the search for the operations of nature. What is the term of nature? God, as is the principle. Where do all things come from? Of the one and only nature.
- .58D. In how many regions is nature divided?
In four main.
What are they?

The dry, the wet, the hot, the cold, which are the four elementary qualities, from which all things derive. How does nature change? Male and female. What is it compared to? Mercury. What idea will you give me of nature?

It is not visible, although it acts visibly, for it is only a volatile spirit, which does its work in the bodies, and which is animated by the universal spirit, which we know in vulgar Masonry, under the respectable emblem of human nature.
A flaming star.
What does it represent positively?
The divine breath, the central and uniiersel Game that vivifies all that exists.
What qualities must the scrutineers of nature have?

They must be such that nature itself, that is to say, true, simple, constant patiens; are the essential characters, which distinguish good Masons, and when these sentiments are already inspired in the candidates in the first initiations, they are prepared beforehand for the acquisition of the qualities necessary for the philosophical class.
What attention should they have next?

Philosophers must consider exactly whether what they propose is according to nature, whether it is possible and feasible; if they want to do something like nature does, they must follow it in every way.

What road should he hold to operate something more excellent than nature has done? One must look at how and by what it improves; one will find that it is always with its like: for example, if one wishes to extend the intrinsic virtue of some metal beyond nature, one must then grasp the metallic nature itself, and know how to distinguish the male and the female in said nature. Where does it contain its seeds?
In the four elements.
What can the Philosopher do with it?

With the germ of the said thing, which is the elixir, or the quintessence much better, and more useful to the artist than nature itself; so, at first, that the Philosopher will have obtained this seed or germ, nature to assist him will be ready to do his duty.

i6o D. What is the germ or seed of  all things? It is the most accomplished and the most perfect decoction and digestion of the thing itself, or rather it is the balm of sulfur, which is the same thing as the radical wet in metals. Who begets this seed, or this germ > R. The four elements, by the will of the Supreme Being, and the imagination of nature. How do the four elements work? By an indefatigable and continuous movement, each of them according to his quality, throwing their seed in the center of the earth, where it is annealed and digested, then pushed out by the laws of movement. What do the Philosophers mean by the center of the earth? A certain void place that they conceive, and where nothing can rest. Where do the four elements cast and rest their qualities or seeds? In the former center, or the margin and circumference of the center, which, after it has taken a due portion, throws the surplus outside, from which are formed the excrements, the drosses, the fires, and even the stones of nature, of this raw stone, emblem of the first Masonic state. Explain this doctrine to me with an example?

Let there be given a well-united table, and on it, in its middle, duly seated and placed any vessel, filled with water only in its outline; then one places several things of various colors, among others that there is particularly salt, observing that each of these things are well divided and set apart, then after one pours the water in the middle, one will see it flow from here and there to meet it. the other passing through the salt will contract salting because; it is certain that the water does not change the places, but the diversity of the places changes the nature of the water; in the same way the seed thrown by the four elements in the center of the earth contracts different modifications because it passes through different places, branches, ducts; so that everything is born according to the diversity of the places, and the seed is born according to the diversity of the places. Earth and pure water would be found, and a pure thing would result from it, and the opposite. How and in what way do the elements beget this seed?

To understand this doctrine well, it must be noted that two elements are serious and pesans, and the other two light, two dry and two wet, yet one extremely dry and the other extremely humid, and besides are masculine and feminine; now, each of them is very quick to produce things similar to itself in its sphere: these four elements never rest, but they act continually in the same way as they do in the same. We may see this process of nature, and know it much more distinctly in the sublime grades which follow it.
What is the real and raw material of metals?

The first matter proper is of double essence, double in itself; nevertheless one without the co-operation of the other does not create a metal; the first and the principal is a moisture of the air, mingled with a warm air, in the form of a greasy water, adhering to every thing, for pure or impure as it may be. How did the Philosophers name this humidity?
Mercury.
By whom is it governed?
By the rays of the Sun and the Moon.
What is the second matter.
It is the heat of the Earth, that is to say, a dry heat which the Philosophers call sulfur.

Does the whole body of matter become a seed? No, but only the eight hundredth part that rests in the center of the same body, as can be seen in the example of a grain of wheat. What is the purpose of the body of matter in relation to the seed? To preserve it from any excessive heat, coldness, humidity or dryness, and generally any harmful weather, against which the material serves as an envelope. Would the Artist, who pretends to reduce the whole body of matter to seed, supposing that he could succeed in it, find any advantage in it? None; on the contrary, his work then becomes absolutely useless, because he can do nothing good as soon as he departs from the process of nature. So what does he have to do? It must release matter from all its impurities; for there is no metal, however puY it may be, unless it has its impurities, one more or less than the other. What is the precise reason for this?
It is because the metals of the vulgar, mainly gold, are absolutely dead, whereas ours, on the contrary, are absolutely alive, and have spirit.
What is the life of metals?
It is nothing but fire, when they are still lying in their .mines.
What is their death? Their death and their life are the same principle, since they also die by fire, but a fusion fire.
How are metals generated in the bowels of the earth?

After the four elements have produced their strength or virtue in the center of the earth, and have deposited their seed, they have been distilled from nature, sublimated to the surface by heat and the action of perpetual motion.
The windj by distilling itself through the pores of the earth, in what does it resolve itself?

It resolves itself into water from which all things are born, and it is then only a moist vapor, from which vapor is then formed the principal principle of all things, and which serves as the first material for the Philosophers.

What, then, is this principal principle, serving as the first material for the children of science in philosophical work? It will be this same matter, which as soon as it is conceived, can absolutely no longer change its form.

Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, the Sun, the Moon, etc. Do they each have different seeds? They all have the same seed; but the place of their birth has been the cause of this difference, although nature has rather completed its work in the procreation of silver than in that of gold, as well as of others. Why is this vapor compared to sulfur?
Because of its internal heat.

It becomes the radical wet of matter. What kind of mercury does it mean that metals are composed of?
This is absolutely understood of the Mercury of the Philosophers, and in no way of the common or vulgar Mercury, which cannot be a seed having in itself its seed like the other metals.

What, then, is to be taken specifically as regards the subject of our subject? One must take the seed alone or fixed grain, and not the whole body which is distinguished as living male, i.e., sulfur and living female, i.e., mercury.

He completed what nature cannot finish because of the rawness of the air, which by its violence filled the pores of each body, not in the bowels of the earth, but in its surface. What correspondence do metals have between them? To understand this correspondence, we must consider the position of the planets, and be careful that Saturn is the highest of all which succeeds Jupiter, then Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury and finally the Moon. It must be observed that the virtues of the planets do not rise, but descend, and experience teaches us that Mars is easily converted into Venus, and not Venus into Mars, as being lower than a sphere: thus Jupiter is easily transmuted into Mercury because Jupiter is higher than; Mercury, this one is the second after the firmament, this one is the second higher than the Earth, and Saturn is the second higher than the Earth. The Philosopher's Stone is nothing but the radical wet of the elements, perfectly purified and brought to a sovereign fixity, which makes it work such great things for health, the life residing only in the radical wet. What is the secret of doing this wonderful work? This secret consists in knowing how to draw from power to act the innate heat, or the fire of nature enclosed in the center of the radical wet. He will then easily conceive that in the generation of all mixed, there is a kind of irradiation, and a separation of light from darkness, in which nature is perpetually imitator of its creator. How many Heavens are there?

Here there is but one, namely, the firmament separating the waters from the waters; yet three are admitted: the first, which is from the top of the clouds, where the rarefied waters stop, and fall down to the fixed stars, and in this space are the planets and the wandering stars.
The second, which is the place of the fixed stars: the third, which is the place of the supereletic waters.
Why does the scarcity of water end in the first heaven, and not rise beyond it?
Because the nature of rarefied things is to rise ever upward, and because God in His eternal laws has assigned to every thing its own sphere.
Why does each celestial body invariably rotate as if around an axis without declining?
It comes only from the first movement that was imprinted on it, just as a heavy mass set in balan, and attached to a simple thread, would always rotate equally, if the movement were always equal.
Why do the higher waters not wet?
This is how a learned chymist can derive more benefit from the science of rarefaction than from any other.
What material is the firmament or the expanse composed of?
The firmament is properly the air, whose nature is much more suitable to light than water.
After separating the waters from the dry and the earth, what did the Creator do to give rise to the generations?

He created a special light for this office, which he placed in the central fire, and tempered this fire by the moisture of the water, and the coldness of the earth, in order to repress its action, and that its heat should be more suitable to the design of its Author.
What is the action of this central fire?

He continually acts on the wet matter which is nearest to him, from which he causes to rise a vapor, which is the mercury of nature, and of the first matter of the three kingdoms. How does nature’s sulfur form?

By the double action or rather reaction of this central fire, on the mercurial steam. How is sea salt made? He must be, as far as possible, a faithful copyist of his creator; in his physical work must make his chaos as it really was; separate light from darkness; form his firmament separating the waters from the waters, and finally accomplish perfectly, following the indicated course, the whole work of creation. With what do we do this great and sublime operation? With a single corpuscle or small body, which contains, so to speak, only feces, dirt, abominations, from which a certain dark and mercurial moisture is extracted, which comprehends in itself all that is necessary to the Philosopher, because he seeks only true mercury. What mercury should be used for the work? Of a mercury which is not so on earth, but which is extracted from bodies, and not from vulgar mercury, as it has been said. Why is the latter not the most appropriate for our work? Because the wise artist must be careful that vulgar mercury does not in itself contain the sufficient amount of sulfur, and that consequently he must work on a body created by nature, in which it will have joined together sulfur and mercury, which the artist must separate. What should he do next? Purify them and join them again. What do you call that body? Raw stone, or chaos, or illiafte, or hyle.

Our mercury, with regard to nature, is twofold, fixed and volatile; with regard to its movement it is twofold also, since it has a movement of ascension, and one of descension: by that of descension, it is the influence of plants, by which it awakens the fçu of dormant nature, and it is its first office before its freezing: by the movement of ascension it is then considered to be vincible.

The mercury of the Philosophers can be considered in four respects; first, it is called the mercury of the bodies, it is precisely the hidden seed: in the second, the mercury of nature; it is the bath or the vase of the Philosophers, in other words the radical wet: in the third, the mercury of nature.
Philosophers, because it is in their shop and in their mining; it is the sphere of

Why do Masons have odd numbers, and namely the septenary in veneration?

Because nature, which delights in its own numbers, is satisfied with the mysterious number of seven, especially in things subordinate, or dependent on the lunar globe; the moon making us see substantially an infinite number of alterations and vicissitudes in this septenary number.
How many operations are there in our work?
There is only one, which is reduced to sublimation, which is nothing else, according to Geber, but the elevation of the dry thing by means of fire with adherence to its own vessel.
What precaution should one take when reading the Hermetic Philosophers?
It is necessary above all to take great care not to take what they say on this subject at the foot of the letter, and according to the sound of the words: For the letter kills, and Vspirit quickens.

When he knows by theory how to draw from a body dissolved by means of a raw spirit, a digestible spirit, which will have to be joined again to the vital oil. Can you explain this theory more clearly? Composition of Metals

It is not arbitrarily that alchemists assert that metals are compound bodies; several examples militate in their favor, recognized by classical chemistry. What is V Ammonium if not a metal composed of Nitrogen and Hydrogen? Ammonia forms its oxide, as potash does Potassium oxide.
Among the metalloids, we have seen that Chlorine, Brome, Iodine, fluorine offer a number of common properties: for example, to form with Hydrogen acid combinations.

Cyanogen, formed of nitrogen and carbon, exhibits identical properties; it combines with hydrogen as a metalloid and forms a hydracid similar to the hydracids of Chlorine, Brome and Iode. It unites with metals and gives binary compounds, cyanides perfectly comparable to chlorides, bromides, iodides. So a complex body behaves exactly like the bodies deemed simple.
